healthyDiets.name: Mediterranean Diet
healthyDiets.description: Emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, nuts, olive oil, and lean protein like fish and poultry.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Grilled salmon with a quinoa salad, cherry tomatoes, cucumbers, feta cheese, and a drizzle of olive oil.

healthyDiets.name: DASH Diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension)
healthyDiets.description: Designed to combat high blood pressure by reducing sodium and eating a variety of foods rich in nutrients that lower blood pressure.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Baked chicken breast, steamed broccoli, and a sweet potato.

healthyDiets.name: Flexitarian Diet
healthyDiets.description: A primarily vegetarian diet that allows for occasional meat and animal products in moderation.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Black bean burgers on whole-wheat buns with avocado and a side salad.

healthyDiets.name: Whole-Foods, Plant-Based Diet
healthyDiets.description: Focuses on minimally processed plant foods: fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, nuts, and seeds.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large bowl of lentil soup with whole-grain bread.

healthyDiets.name: Vegan Diet
healthyDiets.description: Excludes all animal products, including meat, dairy, eggs, and honey.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Tofu scramble with spinach, turmeric, and nutritional yeast, served with whole-grain toast.

healthyDiets.name: Pescatarian Diet
healthyDiets.description: A vegetarian diet that includes fish and seafood.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Seared tuna steak with roasted asparagus and brown rice.

healthyDiets.name: Nordic Diet
healthyDiets.description: Similar to Mediterranean but features foods local to the Nordic countries: berries, root vegetables, fatty fish, oats, and rye.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Baked herring with roasted root vegetables (beets, carrots) and a side of lingonberries.

healthyDiets.name: Okinawan Diet
healthyDiets.description: Based on the traditional eating patterns of Okinawa, Japan, emphasizing sweet potatoes, green vegetables, and soy.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Stir-fried bitter melon (goya) with tofu, egg, and served with a small portion of purple sweet potato.

healthyDiets.name: Traditional Asian Diet
healthyDiets.description: Emphasizes rice, noodles, vegetables, fruits, soy, and fish, with minimal meat and dairy.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Vegetable and tofu stir-fry with brown rice.

healthyDiets.name: Intermittent Fasting (16/8 Method)
healthyDiets.description: Involves cycling between periods of eating and fasting. The 16/8 method has a 16-hour daily fast and an 8-hour eating window.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Meals are not prescribed, but breaking a fast could be with a balanced meal like chicken and vegetables.

healthyDiets.name: Intermittent Fasting (5:2 Diet)
healthyDiets.description: Involves eating normally for 5 days of the week and restricting calories to 500-600 on the other 2 non-consecutive days.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: On a fast day: a large salad with grilled chicken breast and a light vinaigrette.

healthyDiets.name: Mindful Eating
healthyDiets.description: Not a diet but a practice of paying full attention to the experience of eating, without distraction.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Any meal eaten slowly, savoring each bite, and listening to hunger/fullness cues.

healthyDiets.name: Intuitive Eating
healthyDiets.description: A framework that rejects dieting mentality, honors hunger, and makes peace with food.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Choosing foods that both satisfy the body and taste good, without guilt.

healthyDiets.name: Volumetrics Diet
healthyDiets.description: Focuses on eating foods with high water and fiber content (like fruits and vegetables) to feel full on fewer calories.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large portion of vegetable soup and a salad before a main course.

healthyDiets.name: Mayo Clinic Diet
healthyDiets.description: A lifestyle program focused on replacing unhealthy habits with healthy ones, using a food pyramid that prioritizes fruits and vegetables.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large spinach salad with grilled shrimp, berries, and a light yogurt-based dressing.

healthyDiets.name: WW (Weight Watchers)
healthyDiets.description: A points-based system where foods are assigned a value based on calories, sugar, saturated fat, and protein.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A zero-point food meal like grilled chicken breast and steamed vegetables.

healthyDiets.name: Low-Carb Diet (General)
healthyDiets.description: Restricts carbohydrates found in sugary foods, pasta, and bread. Emphasizes protein, fat, and vegetables.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Cheese and vegetable omelet with a side of avocado.

healthyDiets.name: Ketogenic (Keto) Diet
healthyDiets.description: A very low-carb, high-fat diet that puts the body into a metabolic state called ketosis.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Pan-seared steak with a creamy garlic herb sauce and sautéed kale.

healthyDiets.name: Paleo Diet
healthyDiets.description: Focuses on foods presumed to be available to Paleolithic humans: meat, fish, vegetables, fruits, nuts, and seeds. Excludes grains, dairy, and processed foods.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Leafy green salad topped with grilled chicken, avocado, walnuts, and an olive oil dressing.

healthyDiets.name: High-Protein Diet
healthyDiets.description: Prioritizes protein intake to promote satiety, preserve muscle mass, and boost metabolism.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Greek yogurt with protein powder, berries, and a sprinkle of almonds.

healthyDiets.name: Low-FODMAP Diet
healthyDiets.description: Temporarily eliminates fermentable carbs to identify triggers for IBS and digestive symptoms.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Grilled chicken with quinoa and carrots (using garlic-infused oil for flavor instead of whole garlic).

healthyDiets.name: Anti-Inflammatory Diet
healthyDiets.description: Emphasizes foods that reduce inflammation, such as tomatoes, olive oil, green leafy vegetables, nuts, and fatty fish.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Salmon with turmeric and ginger, served with steamed broccoli and a side of blueberries.

healthyDiets.name: DASH-Sodium Diet
healthyDiets.description: A stricter version of the DASH diet with even lower sodium intake for those with significant hypertension.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Homemade oatmeal with berries and cinnamon (no salt added).

healthyDiets.name: Renal Diet (Kidney-Friendly)
healthyDiets.description: Restricts sodium, potassium, and phosphorus to reduce strain on the kidneys for those with kidney disease.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A controlled portion of white rice with a small serving of unmarinated chicken and green beans.

healthyDiets.name: Soft Food Diet
healthyDiets.description: Consists of foods that are soft and easy to chew and swallow, often used after surgery or for dental issues.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Mashed potatoes, pureed butternut squash, and a smoothie.

healthyDiets.name: Gluten-Free Diet
healthyDiets.description: Eliminates the protein gluten, found in wheat, barley, and rye. Essential for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A salad with grilled chicken, chickpeas, and a gluten-free vinaigrette.

healthyDiets.name: Dairy-Free Diet
healthyDiets.description: Eliminates milk and milk products, often due to lactose intolerance or a milk allergy.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Oat milk smoothie with dairy-free protein powder and fruit.

healthyDiets.name: MIND Diet (Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay)
healthyDiets.description: A hybrid of the Mediterranean and DASH diets, specifically targeting brain health to reduce dementia risk.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large salad with leafy greens, blueberries, and a vinaigrette, alongside a serving of baked fish.

healthyDiets.name: Fertility Diet
healthyDiets.description: Often emphasizes plant-based proteins, full-fat dairy, and complex carbs, based on research from the Nurses' Health Study.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Whole-milk Greek yogurt with berries and a sprinkle of flax seeds.

healthyDiets.name: Primal Diet
healthyDiets.description: Similar to Paleo but includes high-quality full-fat dairy and allows for coffee and dark chocolate in moderation.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Omelet cooked in butter with vegetables and cheese, served with a side of berries.

healthyDiets.name: Carnivore Diet
healthyDiets.description: An all-meat diet, consisting solely of animal products like meat, fish, eggs, and limited dairy.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Ribeye steak and scrambled eggs.

healthyDiets.name: Zone Diet
healthyDiets.description: Aims for a specific ratio of macronutrients: 40% carbs, 30% protein, 30% fat at every meal to control inflammation.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A precisely measured plate with 3oz chicken, a large apple, and a small handful of almonds.

healthyDiets.name: Alkaline Diet
healthyDiets.description: Based on the idea that replacing acid-forming foods with alkaline foods can improve health. Focuses on fruits, vegetables, and nuts.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large green smoothie made with spinach, kale, cucumber, and almond milk.

healthyDiets.name: Macrobiotic Diet
healthyDiets.description: A philosophy-based diet that emphasizes whole grains, vegetables, and fermented foods, while minimizing processed foods and animal products.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A bowl of brown rice miso soup with sea vegetables and steamed daikon.

healthyDiets.name: Raw Food Diet
healthyDiets.description: Consists of uncooked, unprocessed foods, often organic. Believed to preserve enzymes and nutrients lost in cooking.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Zucchini noodles with a raw pesto sauce made from basil, pine nuts, and olive oil.

healthyDiets.name: The Engine 2 Diet
healthyDiets.description: A strict, whole-food, plant-based diet that excludes all animal products, added oils, and refined foods.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Oil-free sweet potato and black bean tacos with corn tortillas and fresh salsa.

healthyDiets.name: The Pegan Diet (Paleo-Vegan)
healthyDiets.description: A combination of Paleo and Vegan principles, focusing on plants and high-quality meats while avoiding dairy, grains, and processed foods.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large salad with mixed greens, roasted vegetables, avocado, and a small portion of grilled salmon.

healthyDiets.name: The Blood Type Diet
healthyDiets.description: Suggests that a person's blood type should determine their dietary choices. (Note: Lacks strong scientific evidence).
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Varies significantly by blood type (e.g., Type O: lean meat and vegetables; Type A: plant-based).

healthyDiets.name: The GAPS Diet (Gut and Psychology Syndrome)
healthyDiets.description: An elimination diet designed to heal the gut lining, focusing on bone broth, probiotics, and easily digestible foods.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Homemade bone broth with well-cooked vegetables and boiled meat.

healthyDiets.name: The Sirtfood Diet
healthyDiets.description: Focuses on foods rich in sirtuins, a group of proteins believed to regulate metabolism. Involves initial calorie restriction followed by a maintenance phase.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A green juice made with kale, arugula, parsley, green apple, and matcha powder, alongside a meal featuring buckwheat.

healthyDiets.name: The TLC Diet (Therapeutic Lifestyle Changes)
healthyDiets.description: A plan from the National Institutes of Health to cut cholesterol through diet, exercise, and weight loss.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Oatmeal with strawberries and a plant sterol-fortified milk alternative.

healthyDiets.name: The Ornish Diet
healthyDiets.description: A very low-fat, predominantly vegetarian diet designed to reverse heart disease.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A large bowl of vegetable and bean soup with a whole-grain roll.

healthyDiets.name: The Ayurvedic Diet
healthyDiets.description: An ancient Indian system that tailors food choices to one's dosha (body type: Vata, Pitta, Kapha) to achieve balance.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Varies by dosha (e.g., Kapha: spicy lentil soup; Pitta: cooling cucumber salad).

healthyDiets.name: The DNA Diet
healthyDiets.description: An emerging field of nutrigenomics where dietary recommendations are based on an individual's genetic profile.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Highly personalized (e.g., someone with a gene variant for slow caffeine metabolism would be advised to avoid coffee).

healthyDiets.name: The Climarian Diet
healthyDiets.description: A diet focused on reducing one's carbon footprint and environmental impact by choosing sustainable foods.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: A lentil and vegetable stew made with locally sourced, seasonal produce.

healthyDiets.name: The No-White-Foods Diet
healthyDiets.description: A simple rule-based approach that eliminates refined 'white' foods like white bread, white rice, white pasta, and sugar.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Quinoa bowl with black beans, corn, salsa, and grilled chicken.

healthyDiets.name: The Dukan Diet
healthyDiets.description: A high-protein, low-carb diet divided into four phases: attack, cruise, consolidation, and stabilization.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: During the 'Attack' phase: lean steak and non-fat yogurt.

healthyDiets.name: The South Beach Diet
healthyDiets.description: Focuses on replacing bad carbs and fats with good carbs and fats. Has phases to promote rapid weight loss and maintenance.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Phase 1: grilled vegetables and lean steak.

healthyDiets.name: The Acid Reflux Diet
healthyDiets.description: Avoids common trigger foods like spicy foods, citrus, tomatoes, chocolate, mint, and fried foods.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Oatmeal with bananas and almond milk.

healthyDiets.name: The Anti-Candida Diet
healthyDiets.description: A strict diet that eliminates sugar, gluten, alcohol, and some dairy to prevent the overgrowth of Candida yeast.
healthyDiets.exampleMeal: Steamed broccoli and chicken sautéed in coconut oil.
